newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank targets 4.9-5.8 pct 1997 inflation. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank targets 4.9-5.8 pct 1997 inflation. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects figure in headline and text from 4.9-5.7 pct)
The National Bank of Slovakia said on Thursday that it would aim to keep inflation for the whole of 1997 to between 4.9 to 5.8 percent, and to keep money supply growth under 10.7 percent.
At a news conference introducing the NBS's monetary policy plans for next year, the central bank's governor Vladimir Masar said gross domestic product growth was forecast at about five percent.
"We expect the favourable development of inflation to continue within the range ... but with a slower decrease (of inflation) as it has been so far," Masr said.
Slovak november inflation stood at 5.4 percent, year-on-year, down from 7.9 percent a year ago.
The central bank's key money supply measure, M2, showed 19 percent year-on-year growth at the end of September.
Slovak GDP growth was 7.1 percent, year-on-year, for the first half of 1996.
